title: Moon base: fourteen days of night (one take, the sky of 8 January 2039, a fuller base)
note: Nov 24, fifth version. One camera take, no cut and no transition effect, 25.0 s. The picture is NASA's 4K concept animation 'Living and Working on the Moon' (May 2026), source frames 165-329 run there and back; night_fall.py (specs/night_v15_one.json) works on a 3510x1920 strip of it and moves a 1080x1920 frame across that strip at 1:1. The sky is computed for 8 January 2039, 14:00 UTC, the real moment closest to NASA's frame (JPL DE440 ephemeris through skyfield; earth_face.py): the Sun at ecliptic longitude 288.08 degrees, the Earth 21.57 degrees from it (drawn 0.8 degrees from where NASA put it), Mars 1.3 degrees from the Earth's centre, Mercury 9.8 degrees from the Sun. Faint light is on one scale (S10 units): NASA's Deep Star Maps 2020 (64k) calibrated on catalogue stars; the zodiacal light from Clementine's measured fit (arXiv astro-ph/0204111, eq. 5), flattened toward the poles by our assumption; the Earth's night side lit by the Moon (our arithmetic), shown with one day of NASA GIBS satellite imagery (VIIRS, 8 January 2024: that day's clouds, not 2039's). The astronaut is from NASA's Moon Base November update (4K, real frames only, 80% speed), held still (astro_stab.py), cut out (astro_cut.py) and stood behind the foreground rock (rock_track.py); he is in the mountain's shadow like the ground and lit by his own helmet lamps. Also ours: the travelling shadow, the night, every lamp and status light, two landers with their attitude jets, dust at touchdown, spacecraft in low orbit, four people on foot with their shadows, a rover's light far off, grain and lens fall-off. Credit NASA; NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio (Deep Star Maps 2020; Gaia DR2: ESA/Gaia/DPAC); NASA GIBS/Worldview (VIIRS, Suomi NPP); star positions HYG database (CC BY-SA 4.0). Sound effects are synthesised (sfx.py). In this version: the view is checked against a real place (moon_site.py): about 85 S, 17-21 W, where at that moment the Sun stood 4.5 degrees up and the Earth 4.2; the Earth's sunlit crescent carries that moment's face with the red of sunset along the day-night line, and its night side the lights of its cities (NASA Black Marble, GIBS); 1,495 catalogue stars to magnitude 8.6; ten more work lights on NASA's modules, eight more people on foot, a second rover's light, two more spacecraft in orbit; the ground's own fine relief shown more strongly in the dark; a film's red glow round strong lights and a light sharpening.

shots.job: This shot follows one night at the base in a single take: the Sun low over the ridge as a lander comes in and the ridge's shadow crosses the base; lamps, helmet lamps and stars in the dark under a crescent Earth; first light on the high ridge and across the plain; the shadow coming back as the camera returns to the Sun and a second lander arrives. So the viewer lives through the night the sentences describe. (NASA concept animation; everything listed in the note added)

lines.say: On most of the Moon, night lasts about fourteen days. Small landers have survived it by mostly shutting down.
A crew can't do that. Life support has to keep running, and no base has yet run through a lunar night.
text: Life support has to keep running,
